Revised after review: the Argos-and-Acte disc was subtracted for all of 225-211 although the text limits it to 225-224 (ledger 13 regains Argos in 224); this keyframe now holds 225 only and 224 onward is split into achaean-league_-224 and achaean-league_-223.

'In 224 BC, while Antigonus was liberating the occupied cities in the Peloponnese' (Aratus page); Aratus found Argos had 'fallen already to an internal uprising' (Aratus page) and Cleomenes left the Isthmus, so Corinth 'fell to Antigonus' (ledger 12). Neither the Aratus nor the Cleomenean War page puts a year on the Argive revolt itself: 224 is the year of Antigonus's liberation of the cities (ledger 13, confidence 2). Megara is still in: it leaves in 223.

The Cleomenean War infobox lists 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon', and the page has Antigonus take Heraea and Orchomenus in early spring 223 (Cleomenes had taken Orchomenus in 229 and Heraea about 227): not subtracted here, because the shape does not draw them as separate cells and the pages give no coordinates; antigonid-dynasty should carry them. The gazetteer's Megara disc is below Cliopatria's cell size, so subtracting it changes no cell; it is kept for the record.

Messene, Corone, Sparta and Pagae 'were joined by conquest' and Hypana in Elis is listed as a later member (Achaean League page, no dates): 191 is a bridging year, confidence 1 (ledger 25, 26); the league held Messene by 183 (ledger 27). ledger.note: 280 (text '281/0 BC'; infobox 'Re-founded 280 BC'): 'The regional Achaean League was revived in 281/0 BC by the communities of Dyme, Patrae, Pharae, and Tritaea'.

275: 'Around the year 275 BC, the people expelled the Macedonian garrison and the city joined the new Achaean League' (Aigio page); 'joined in 275 by Aegium, which controlled the important sanctuary of Zeus Homarios'. The other eastern Achaean cities (Bura, Cerynea, Aigeira, Pellene) followed undated.
275: Aegium (38.251 N, 22.081 E) 'became the Achaean assembly place' and 'remained their capital until the Roman conquest in 146 BC'. Year taken from its accession.
251: Aratus 'overthrew the tyranny in his native city and brought it into the Achaean League'; the first non-Achaean member.

243: Aratus 'captured Corinth and the fortress of Acrocorinth in 243 BC in a daring night attack' from the Macedonian garrison; 'After its capture by Aratus, Corinth also joined the Achaean League' (Aratus page).
243 ('shortly afterwards'): Corinth 'was followed shortly afterwards by Megara, Troezen, and Epidaurus'. Dated to the year of Corinth's capture; the pages give no separate year.

235: Lydiades, tyrant of Megalopolis, 'decided to give up his power by joining the Achaean League' ('That year', 235); 'Corinth was followed by Megalopolis in 235 BC and Argos in 229 BC' (Achaean League page).

Soon after 235 (undated: 'Orchomenus and Mantinea soon followed suit'): the eastern Arcadian cities. Confidence 1 for the year; both were Spartan again by 229-226 (Mantinea had an Achaean garrison in 226).

229: 'Argos in 229 BC'; 'Aristomachus of Argos also abandoned the Macedonian alliance and joined the Achaean League' (Aratus page). Athens, freed of its garrison the same year, 'refused the invitation to join'. Hermione, Phlius and Aegina (also members by 225) are not dated on the pages.

region.text: Arcadia and the Argolid, the Cleomenean War zone

ledger.note: 229/228 to 222: the Cleomenean War (infobox 'Sparta, Elis vs. Achaean League, Macedonia'). In 229 Cleomenes took 'Tegea, Mantineia, Caphyae, and Orchomenus in Arcadia, which had allied with the Aetolian League' and 'the Athenaeum, near Belbina' (228); Aratus 'took Caphyae'. Rule 6 blend; the antigonid-dynasty dossier carries its own 224-222 pair with the same counterpart string.

226: 'In 226 BC, the citizens of Mantinea appealed to Cleomenes to expel the Achaean garrison from the city'; he 'removed the garrison that night'. Cleomenes also 'captured the city of Lasium and presented it to the Elians'.

region.text: Argos, Cleonae, Phlius, Hermione, Troezen, Epidaurus and Corinth (the Achaean garrison holding out on Acrocorinth)

ledger.note: 225 (year from the narrative): Cleomenes took Argos during the Nemean Games, the Argives 'accepted a garrison, delivered twenty hostages to Cleomenes and became Spartan allies'; 'Cleonae, Phlius, Hermione, Troezen, and Epidaurus surrendered to him', 'The Corinthians did surrender the city to Cleomenes', who 'besieged the Achaean garrison on Acrocorinth'.

224: 'Aratus agreed to give Acrocorinth to Antigonus in return for his support'; 'Cleomenes gave up the Isthmus and Corinth fell to Antigonus'. Infobox 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon'. The antigonid-dynasty dossier carries the matching gain.
224: 'The Argives revolted against Cleomenes, and the Achaean reinforcements took the whole city except the citadel'; with Antigonus's advance the Acte cities returned. Year from the narrative.
223: 'Megara deserted the Achaean League and joined the Boeotian Confederacy', cut off by Macedonian Corinth. Megara's return (192, 'Pagae' added later) is not dated on the pages.

Summer 222: Sellasia, 'Decisive Macedonian-Achaean victory'; 'Antigonus became the first non-Spartan general to occupy Sparta' and 'did not force Sparta to join the League' (Cleomenean War page). Tegea, Orchomenus, Mantinea, Heraea and Telphusa had been taken by Antigonus in 'the early spring of 223 BC'; Orchomenus and Heraea stayed Macedonian (infobox), the rest returned to the Achaean sphere (Mantinea as Antigoneia, not on the pages).

region.text: western Achaea and Arcadia, raided by the Aetolians

ledger.note: Spring 220 to 217: Aetolian troops 'pillaged the countryside of several Achaean cities, namely Patras and Pharae' and burned 'the Arcadian city of Cynaetha'; 'In the summer of 219 BC Sparta attacked Achaea from the south'. Rule 6 blend.

Winter 219/218: Philip V 'stormed the city of Psophis and handed it over to his Achaean ally Aratus the Younger'; 'The same procedure was used at Lasion'. Infobox 'Psophis and Lasion to Achaea'. Elis, the Aetolians' ally, is the counterpart (free text; no Elis dossier exists).
217: the Peace of Naupactus, 'every side should maintain what it currently possessed'.

Winter 198/197: Argos went over to Philip V when the league 'voted to join the anti-Macedonian alliance' at Sicyon (198), and 'Philip handed Argos to Nabis, who then engineered a revolution there and agreed at Mycenae to stop attacking the Achaeans'. Nabis gained 'control of the important city of Argos as the price of his alliance with the Macedonians' (Nabis page).

197: 'Corinth rejoined' (membership list); 'The Romans reportedly offered the city of Corinth to the League as an inducement' (Second Macedonian War page). Acrocorinth kept a Roman garrison until 194 (next pair).
197-194: 'Roman garrisons remained in Corinth, Chalcis, and Demetrias until 194 BC' (rule 4 hatch over the Achaean colour).

195: 'Flamininus ordered Nabis to give Argos back to the Achaeans, or face war with Rome'; after the Spartan defeat 'Nabis was forced to surrender both Argos and the port of Gytheum'. Who received Gytheum and the Laconian coast is not said (the free Laconians are not drawn).
194: Flamininus withdraws the garrisons of Corinth, Chalcis and Demetrias.

192: Nabis 'was assassinated in 192 BC by the Aetolian League'; afterwards Philopoemen 'compelled the Spartans to join the Achaean League' (Nabis page; 'Philopoemen forced Sparta to become a member state', Philopoemen page, undated). In 188 Philopoemen 'demolished the wall that the former tyrant of Sparta, Nabis, had built around Sparta'. Counterpart peloponnesian-league is the sibling dossier for Sparta, which ends in 192 with this event.

191 (bridging year; no date on the page, which says Messene, Corone, Sparta and Pagae 'were joined by conquest'): Messene and Messenia enter the league. The Roman-Seleucid War page lists Messene on the Seleucid side (infobox, 192-188), and the league held Messene by 183 (contest below). The messene dossier carries the matching loss and its dissolve.

191 (bridging year; the page dates none of them): Hypana in Elis is listed as a later member and Elis itself is named as a hostile independent state, not a member; the Roman-Seleucid War page lists Elis on the Seleucid side. greek-city-states /ledger/68 carries the matching 191 loss of 'Messene and Elis' with the rest of the Peloponnese; a dossier for Elis would be the truer counterpart (counterparts_needing_dossiers).
183: 'Dinocrates, who strongly opposed Philopoemen, encouraged Messene to revolt against the League'; Philopoemen was captured and killed there (183 or 182). Rule 6 blend over Messenia.
182: 'On hearing of his death, the members of the Achaean League joined forces to capture Messene' (Lycortas). Year from Philopoemen's death (183/182).

150: 'hostilities between Sparta and the League flared up again'; in 147 the Roman envoy Orestes 'tried to announce the forced reduction of the Achaean League to its original, narrow grouping'. Rule 6 blend over Laconia.
146: the Roman settlement ends the dispute with the league's dissolution.

146: Metellus 'decisively defeated' Critolaos 'at the Battle of Scarpheia'; Diaeus's army was routed at Corinth, and the Romans 'destroyed the city'; 'the Greek states were grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia'.
146: the Romans 'razed Corinth and dissolved the League'; 'all leagues and other political entities were dissolved'. Infobox 'Roman annexation of mainland Greece'. Cliopatria ends the row in 145.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Achaean League' (-279..-145) is right in outline but systematically late and, after 206, badly undersized: Sicyon (251), Corinth and the Acte (243), Megalopolis (235) each appear four to eight years after the pages date them, and the 206-145 polygon (11.8 k km2) never shows the league's doubling to the whole Peloponnese (Argos back 195, Sparta 192, Messene and Elis c. 191). The Cleomenean War (229-222) is drawn as uninterrupted growth where the league in fact lost Mantinea (226), Argos, the Acte and Corinth (225) and then ceded Acrocorinth, Heraea and Orchomenus to Macedon (224). Start moved to 280 (infobox; text '281/0'), end to 146. Disagreements: Philopoemen's death 183 (lead) or 182 (strategos table). Not on the pages and left at confidence 1 or omitted: the eastern Achaean cities' accession (275-270s), Hermione, Phlius and Aegina, Mantinea as Antigoneia (223), Megara's return, Messene and Elis's accession year, the Laconian coastal towns of 195, and the Roman settlement's internal terms of 146. Counterparts given as free text that need dossiers: Sparta to 192 is the sibling dossier peloponnesian-league (Sparta's state, -800..-192); the secession of 150-146 has no dossier, Elis, the Boeotian League, Messene. Gazetteer: Achaea, Arcadia, Argolis, Laconia, Messenia, Elis and Corinthia do not exist as regions and Argos, Sicyon, Megara, Epidaurus, Troezen, Megalopolis, Mantinea and Psophis are not places; radii on coordinates stand in and are reported. Revised 2026-10-19 after review: the keyframes from 239 on are now split by year (239-236; 235; 234-231; 225; 224; 223-211; 210-207; 206-199; 198; 197-196; 195-193; 192; 191-165) so that Megalopolis and Orchomenus-Mantinea, Argos (lost 198, back 195), Corinth (out 224-197), Megara (out from 223), Sparta (192) and the whole Peloponnese (from 191) appear in their own years; ledger 25 is split into Messenia (counterpart messene) and Elis (counterpart greek-city-states); the First Macedonian War and the Roman-Seleucid War are listed in wars with the league's part. Left open: the Argive revolt has no year on the pages (224 follows Antigonus's liberation of the cities); Heraea and Orchomenus pass to Macedon in early spring 223 (Cleomenean War page) and are not subtracted; Megara's return and Pagae's accession are undated.
